analysis.title: DB CoTD: Just Another Manic (Trillion Dollar) Monday
key_insights: Deutsche Bank published its World Outlook for 2027, titled 'Great Expectations, but Risky Business', with all economists and strategists contributing.
Equity strategist Binky Chadha forecasts the S&P 500 reaching 9,000 by end-2027.
Nvidia added $952bn of market cap in one day, after at one point being on course to add a full $1tn, which would have been a first for any company.
The Nvidia move was more than double the second largest single-company move in history, Microsoft's $450bn in July of this year.
Nvidia holds four other spots in the top ten largest daily market cap gains, and all top ten moves occurred in the last 2.5 years.
Apple and Nvidia are the two largest companies at around $5tn and $4tn market cap respectively, and 13 companies exceed $1tn.

Historical context: IBM was the largest S&P 500 company in 1981 at $33.7bn ($123.8bn in real terms), Microsoft peaked at $601bn at end-1999 ($1.2tn real), and Apple became the first $1tn US company in August 2018.
DB says the factors hoped to drive markets higher in 2027 are also the ones posing the biggest risks, so it expects another high-octane year.

market_movers.rationale: Nvidia added $952bn of market cap in a single day, the largest single-company daily gain on record, and is now around $4tn in market cap.

macro_indicators.interpretation: DB's equity strategist sees substantial upside, supported by mega-cap tech strength, though concentration raises risk.

risk_factors: The drivers expected to lift markets in 2027 are the same ones that pose the biggest risks.
Extreme concentration in a handful of mega-cap names means daily moves in them heavily influence global markets.
charts_described: Chart shows the value of the largest S&P 500 company at year-end each year since 1981 in nominal and real terms, with IBM at $33.7bn in 1981 ($123.8bn real), Microsoft at $601bn in 1999 and about $333bn in 2007.
vol_and_positioning: Concentration in the largest names is extreme, with 13 companies above $1tn and single-day moves of nearly $1tn in one stock, which adds index-level volatility risk.
